speaker: Doctor
text: To help me narrow this down, have you noticed any changes in your sense of touch, muscle weakness, or balance issues like a staggering gait? Also, have you experienced any numbness or tingling in your hands or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: That combination of progressive gait disturbance, urinary incontinence, and dysarthria is highly suggestive of a spinal cord or brainstem lesion. Given your age and the chronicity, have you noticed any back pain, leg stiffness, or issues with bowel control as well? Also, have you had any recent falls or head injuries?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical and Thoracic Spine, and MRI Brainstem. REQUEST IMAGES for both. Have you noticed any visual disturbances like double vision, or any weakness in your arms specifically?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS (Requested MRI Cervical, Thoracic Spine, and Brainstem images are not available in the provided dataset; existing MRI Brain and Spinal Cord report shows findings consistent with neurodegenerative processes in the brainstem, cerebellum, and basal ganglia).

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Unremarkable. No known chronic diseases. Social history: Occasionally consumes alcohol. Non-smoker. Works as a bank clerk.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent infections, fever, weight loss, vision changes or seizures. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple System Atrophy (Shy-Drager Syndrome).
